hook_text: A healer who looks at the body, the mind, the family and the ancestors all at once. How does indigenous healing work?
clip_script: eShowe, Heritage Month. A traditional healer explains her work. Some illnesses have physical causes: injuries, spoiled food, dirty water, snakebites. Many people also believe some illnesses have spiritual causes, linked to the ancestors. Herbalists treat with plants. Diviners, often called by the ancestors, seek the cause through bones, dreams and ceremonies. Healing means caring for the whole person. Today, the law recognises traditional healers, and many people visit both healers and clinics.
visual_style: Whiteboard circle showing a person at the centre, surrounded by body, mind, family, community and ancestors, then a herbalist's plants and a diviner's bones, then a clinic and a healer side by side.
mood: Respectful and thoughtful, like listening to an elder.
pacing: Gentle and clear, explaining beliefs carefully and respectfully, one idea at a time.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and explain in your own words how indigenous healing treats the whole person.
